clue.text: African disease is avoided?

indicators.note: avoided means these letters are left out of the disease's name

parts.note: beriberi is a vitamin-deficiency disease
read as the plural of the letter I: two I's, so both copies go

explanation.surface: A question about whether some African illness has been escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 'is' as I's, two copies of the letter I, both dropped from the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berbers are an indigenous people of North Africa, so a Berber is an African.

clue.text: Father abandons French car carrying one dish

indicators.note: carrying means the letters hold the one inside them
abandons means the father leaves the word French

parts.note: taken as written
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
Lada is a Russian make of car
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A priest leaves his French car holding one meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French car' looks like a Renault or Citroen; in fact French loses its Fr and the car is the Russian Lada.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican tortilla rolled round a filling, a dish.

clue.text: Liberal deserting Midlands region for more remote one?

definitions.note: a more remote region, the noun form of the answer

indicators.note: deserting means the Liberal leaves the region's name

parts.note: the Black Country is the industrial area of the West Midlands near Birmingham

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician abandons the Midlands for somewhere more out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Country is an industrial district of the English West Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Backcountry is sparsely populated land far from towns, a region more remote than an industrial one.

clue.text: River near tree bordering a field

indicators.note: near means the river is placed beside what follows
bordering means the tree runs round the letter A

parts.note: elm is a tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A river close to a tree on the edge of a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' looks like a meadow, but it is the abstract sense: a sphere of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or area of activity, as is a field of study.

clue.text: 25s for example bracing ship faced with small forces

indicators.note: the ship-and-trees part is fronted by the small letter, so it goes first

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: bracing means holding firm on either side, so the trees surround the ship

parts.note: 25 is ELDER, and elders are trees
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Elders supporting a ship under minor loads, like an engineering report on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 25 Down (ELDER) is the tree, not the church elder; the trees wrap round the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering, stresses are the internal loads or pressures acting on a structure, a sense close to forces.

clue.text: Beat shy opener for bounce, missing wicket

indicators.note: missing means the wicket letter is left out

parts.note: to shy is to throw

indicators.note: opener for means the first letter of bounce

parts.note: B is the first letter of bounce

explanation.surface: A cricket shy that misses the stumps, with the opener ducking a bouncer.
explanation.walkthrough: W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a pulse or rhythmic beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: The same European bird passing over India

indicators.note: passing over means skipping, so India is left out of the bird

parts.note: the quail is a game bird
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A migrating European bird flying over India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing over' looks like a flight path, but it means omitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are equal are identical in amount or value, i.e. the same.

clue.text: Hardly any conform to metric system with tonnes

parts.note: a line of verse scans when it fits the metre
T is the abbreviation for tonnes

explanation.surface: Few people comply with the metric system when it comes to tonnes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metric system' suggests weights and measures; here it is poetic metre.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, so scant attention is hardly any attention.

clue.text: Lesbian perhaps seen topless? That's defamation

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a Lesbian is an inhabitant of the Greek island of Lesbos, so an islander

explanation.surface: Calling someone a topless lesbian would be defamatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L matters: a Lesbian is from Lesbos.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander is spoken defamation, a false statement harming a reputation.

clue.text: Excellent returns shown by two accounts in plant

parts.note: AC is account, twice

indicators.note: returns means the word for excellent is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI

explanation.surface: A firm's good returns appear in two sets of accounts at its plant.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI in crosswords, the 1 standing in for I. 'Plant' looks like a factory but is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a thorny tree or shrub, the wattle, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Commotion in dictator's steep ditch

indicators.note: in dictation, i.e. spoken aloud, so the brow is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the brow of a hill is its steep top edge
a ha-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a fence round a park

explanation.surface: An uproar in a tyrant's sheer moat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a tyrant, but here it is someone dictating, so the pieces are heard. A ha-ha is a landscaping ditch on British country estates.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or uproar, a synonym of commotion.

clue.text: Search among adult bodies adrift at sea

indicators.note: among means the search word sits inside the other letters
adrift means the words adult bodies are drifting loose and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: Searching for adult bodies floating at sea after a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adrift at sea' reads as one maritime phrase, but 'adrift' is the anagram signal and 'at sea' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea means bewildered, which is what discombobulated means: thoroughly confused.

clue.text: Work too hard in connection with duty

parts.note: over means about, concerning
a duty is a tax

explanation.surface: Overworking oneself in the line of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtax someone is to make excessive demands on them, overworking them.

clue.text: Criminal clue about northern pawnbroker

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the northern letter
criminal means the letters of clue are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal's tip-off concerning a northern pawnbroker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle was a slang nickname for the pawnbroker, to whom goods were taken for loans.

clue.text: A park pitch reconstructed around area — it's official

indicators.note: around means the rebuilt letters surround the area letter
reconstructed means the letters of a park pitch are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Rebuilding a park's pitch around a space is a council official's job.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparatchik is a Communist Party functionary, now any bureaucratic official.

clue.text: Planet almost consumed in flood

indicators.note: almost means the planet's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Saturn is a planet
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A planet nearly swallowed up in a deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to soak or fill completely, the same sense as flood used as a verb.

clue.text: Potato in Indian fine, or a pudding served up cold?

parts.note: aloo is the Hindi word for potato, familiar from Indian menus

explanation.surface: A menu offering Indian potato or a chilled dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two routes: 'or a pudding served up' gives A plus FOOL upside down, a fool being a fruit-and-cream dessert. Both lead to the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof is cool and distant in manner, i.e. cold towards others.

clue.text: Secret writing on hot image that's reversed

indicators.note: that's reversed means the whole run of letters before it is read backwards

parts.note: re means on, concerning
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: Coded text written over a heat-sensitive picture that has been flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a code, a system of secret writing used to hide a message.

clue.text: Established measures nearly all acknowledge

parts.note: ens are printers' units of measure

indicators.note: nearly all means the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: to concede is to acknowledge

explanation.surface: Settled measures that nearly everyone admits.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's unit of width, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensconced means settled firmly in place, i.e. established.

clue.text: Needlework that liberates husband as well!

indicators.note: liberates means the word that lets go of one of its letters

parts.note: taken as written
too means as well

explanation.surface: A sewing project that frees the husband too!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needlework' suggests embroidery, but the tattooist's needle is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is made by pricking ink into skin with needles, so it is needlework of a sort.

clue.text: Person leaving the demesne — that chap having departed?

definitions.note: leaving in the sense of bequeathing by will

indicators.note: having departed means the chap leaves the word the

parts.note: taken as written
he is that chap
a demesne is a landed estate

explanation.surface: Someone leaving the estate, the man of the house having died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' suggests going away, but it means leaving property in a will; 'departed' hints at death too.
explanation.definitionFit: A testate is someone who has made a valid will, leaving property to heirs.

clue.text: Speculator taking time with gold in robbery

indicators.note: in means the gold sits inside the robbery word

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone takes their time over a gold robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorist speculates, forming hypotheses rather than proven facts, so is a speculator in that sense.

clue.text: In which no axe cut yet if so ordered?

definitions.text: In which no axe cut yet if so ordered?

indicators.note: ordered means the preceding words are put into a new order

parts.words: no axe cut yet if so
parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A situation where the executioner's axe has not yet fallen, if the authorities say so.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and a description: under a court order the axe has not yet been used.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay of execution postpones an execution by official order, so the condemned is spared for now.

clue.text: Room at the top simple and elegant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a room directly under the roof
second meaning: in the restrained classical style of Attica, ancient Athens

explanation.walkthrough: 'Room at the top' sounds like the novel title about ambition; it is just the top-floor room.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a loft space and the plain, refined taste associated with Athens.

clue.text: Maybe G8 leaders to end talks after month?

indicators.note: the leading letters come after the month
leaders means the first letters of end talks

parts.note: E and T are the first letters of end and talks; to is a link

explanation.surface: Leaders of the G8 wrapping up talks after a month of summitry.
explanation.walkthrough: G8 looks like the group of nations, but it is eight of something; OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, so the eight-member G8 is an example.

clue.text: Wifeless worker at seam finding ancestor?

indicators.note: wifeless means without W, the abbreviation for wife

parts.note: a welder joins metal at a seam

explanation.surface: A bachelor miner at the coal seam tracing his forebears.
explanation.walkthrough: The seam looks like a coal seam, but it is a welded join.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a senior or forebear, so in the sense of one who came before it serves as ancestor.

clue.text: Press covering last letter from George Best

indicators.note: covering means the press word goes round the letter

parts.note: to cram is to press or pack in

indicators.note: last letter from means the final letter of George

parts.note: E is the final letter of George

explanation.surface: Newspapers reporting on George Best's last words.
explanation.walkthrough: George Best was a famous footballer; here 'Best' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, the best.

clue.text: Bent coppers ousting first team's leader from position

indicators.note: ousting means the coppers take the place of the team's leader

parts.note: an attitude is a posture or position

indicators.note: first says it is the earlier of the two matching letters in position that goes
leader means the opening letter of team's

parts.note: T is the opening letter of team's
p is pence, copper coins

explanation.surface: Corrupt police kick the captain out of the team's position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent coppers' reads as crooked police, but 'Bent' is the definition and coppers are pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural talent or inclination, which is what an aptitude is.

clue.text: Moral code set out when gathering here in Rome

indicators.note: gathering means the rearranged letters collect the Latin word inside them
out means the letters of set are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
hic is Latin for here

explanation.surface: Rules of conduct laid down when assembling in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are the principles of right conduct, a moral code.

clue.text: Retired sleuth visiting Alpine ridge and so on

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the whole construction is read backwards
visiting means the sleuth is inside the ridge

parts.note: an arete is a sharp mountain ridge
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A retired detective visits a mountain ridge, and so forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' seems to describe only the sleuth, but it turns round the sleuth and the ridge together.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin for 'and the rest', used to mean and so on.

clue.text: Fuss after Kipling hero backs emperor

indicators.note: the fuss comes after the hero
backs means the hero's name runs backwards

parts.note: Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel
ado is fuss

explanation.surface: A commotion as a Kipling character supports a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikado was a historical title of the Japanese emperor, familiar from the Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
